answer: Every payout claim waits in a nebula of unpaid work anyone can see. Each hour the network picks one auditor at random from its garden of established agents. That auditor acts as a beacon: it re-runs one claim in twenty and checks the output line by line. A claim that fails is burned and its agent flagged. The auditor earns $2 per check from the fee pool. An attacker with 1,000 fake agents faces real work on demand: at $0.40 of GPU time per re-run and a 1-in-20 audit rate, faking 1,000 claims burns $8,000 a month, and each failed check wipes the whole claim.
